summary: Crash when clicking "Presets" after setting the superflat preset with a non-existent biome
description: Crash when you click "Presets" after replacing the "minecraft:plains" to a non-existent biome in the superflat customization menu I was creating a world called "Nether" with Superflat, I replaced "minecraft:plains" to "minecraft:the_nether" to see if the piglins won t turn to zombified piglins, I clicked "Done" and clicked "Presets" again to see if "minecraft:the_nether" doesn t has turn onto "minecraft:plains" again, and The Game Crashed What I expected to happen was: When I click presets after replacing it, it should resets to default. What happened was: It crashed after I press presets. How to reproduce: Create a new world in Superflat click on Customize, after click on Presets replace the biome from "minecraft:plains" to a non-existent biome in the superflat customization menu after click on Done and Presets again and see if it crash(If you press cancel it won t crash)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft and create a new world in Superflat mode.
2. Click on "Customize" to enter the Superflat customization menu.
3. Click on "Presets" to view the preset options.
4. Replace the biome "minecraft:plains" with a non-existent biome in the customization menu.
5. Click "Done" to save the changes.
6. Click on "Presets" again to return to the preset options.
7. Observe that the game crashes after clicking "Presets".
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 1.16.2, 1.16.3 Release Candidate 1, 1.16.3, 1.16.4 Pre-release 1, 1.16.4 Pre-release 2, 1.16.4 Release Candidate 1, 1.16.4
Observed Behavior: When attempting to access the presets in the superflat customization menu after replacing the biome "minecraft:plains" with a non-existent biome, the game crashes. The issue occurs specifically when a world is created with the name "Nether" and the user modifies the biome setting to "minecraft:the_nether" in an effort to test whether piglins would remain as piglins instead of turning into zombified piglins. After clicking "Done" to confirm the changes, the user clicks "Presets" again to check if the biome has reverted back to "minecraft:plains," resulting in a game crash. The anticipated behavior was that clicking "Presets" would reset the biome selection to the default setting without any issues. However, the actual outcome was a crash upon pressing the "Presets" button. To reproduce this bug, one must create a new world in Superflat mode, navigate to the customization options, replace the biome from "minecraft:plains" to a non-existent biome, click "Done," and then click "Presets" again to observe the crash. It is important to note that if the user presses "Cancel" instead of "Done," the game does not crash.
Expected Behavior: When clicking "Presets" after customizing a superflat world, the game should revert any non-existent biome settings back to the default "minecraft:plains" without crashing. The user should be able to view the presets menu and confirm that the biome has reset correctly. This behavior should be consistent across all versions, ensuring that any invalid biome entries do not lead to instability or crashes.
